title: Bunk in a rough Hell's Kitchen bar with Kratka
summary: Blumberg finds Bunk in a tough bar, where talk of Australia wins over the hostile bartender and then the patrons turn on Kratka.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: Thank you, my pardon. Go ahead. I went down there, and he wasn't in the apartment, and I was scouting around the neighborhood and found him in the neighborhood bar. And there was one of these bars frequented by the rough types of the neighborhood, which was mostly truck drivers and steam fitters and people. That was over on the west side, I think, wasn't it? Yeah. Or 8th Avenue, was it? Probably was, yeah.
I think about 11th Street or 13th Street, anyway.
It was a basement apartment, that's all I remember.
I never did see the place, but I used to get letters from Bill, especially. Yeah. Bunk hardly ever wrote in those days. When he was on the road, he hardly ever wrote a letter.

It was sort of a tough... almost the edge of Hell's Kitchen, as they called it. Yeah. Farther there on that west side is where the Irish... not that the Irish are necessarily rough, but down here they have the Irish Channel. They have, by reputation, it's supposed to be a tough section for some reason, and Hell's Kitchen, the Irish part of New York is, too. It's a little bit too far south to be able to go ahead and it was a tough section.

Yeah, and it was a tough bar, and I went in and there was Bunk standing at the bar, and I don't know, he was drinking something there, and I guess it was about 2 in the afternoon or 1 in the afternoon. I... this was when I was living at Kratka's, and I was supposed to meet Kratka later on. Bernie de Kratka lived for the... He lived down around the Lancy Street area.
On the east side down there.
I couldn't remember if he was up on 3rd Avenue or someplace. Another friend of ours lived up that way. I forgot.
Harold, I think, or somebody lived up there.
No, another fellow. I can't remember his name. Anyway, go ahead.
You're talking about over at the saloon you went to and the... Uh, yeah, so...

...the inner loft bars. Uh, Bunk was standing there and the rest of the people, of course he was the only Negro in the bar, and the rest of the people, these rough types, they seemed to be very hostile toward him, and I was full of apprehension, you know, as I grasped the situation. And it seemed like Bunk was going to overstep the bounds of good judgment, you know, and get himself into some kind of scrape there, so I was a little scared, and I went up to him. And he was telling some kind of story to the bartender and waggling his finger. He'd get very expansive at times like this, and he'd have his hat over on the side. That was his trademark when he was out drinking, he'd have this Homburg cocked over the side, and he'd be standing at the bar waggling his finger at the bartender and telling some kind of story, and I guess he was just getting grunts, you know, and cold stares as a response. But before long, he started talking about different places around the world, and he started talking about some place in Australia. I guess it was one of the big cities, maybe Melbourne or Sydney or one of those places. But he started talking about a hotel or something in that city, and the bartender suddenly became interested, you know, and they got to talking. And it turns out that the bartender had come from that city, and that Bunk knew his mother, you know, and Bunk mentioned her name and described her, and the guy said, Yeah, yeah, that was my mother. Apparently she ran the lounge in a hotel or something, or Bunk had worked for her or something like that. But all of a sudden it was a great warm reunion, you know, type situation, the whole feeling of the thing changed. And everybody was slapping each other on the back, you know, this kind of thing. And Bunk was describing, you know, in perfect detail things about the place that the bartender was saying, yeah, yeah, agreeing with him. And at this point Kratka comes in, and Bunk is feeling particularly playful now, and starts sparring around with Kratka, you know. Kratka is a very well-built guy, very broad shoulders and powerful build, and Bunk was challenging him to a fight, very playfully. Yeah. But the next thing we knew, he was kind of sparring around and throwing a couple punches, you know, and Kratka was just trying to defend himself, and being backed up to a table there. And all of a sudden, the bartender is coming around the bar, and he's warning Kratka not to touch that old man, you know, or he's going to suffer dire consequences. And poor Irv didn't know what to do. He just walked into the place, and it looked like he was going to have the whole clientele on top of him. They were all for Bunk. Yeah, that's right. Don't you dare touch that old man, you know. And Kratka hadn't lifted a hand.
